skill.name: writing-fragments
skill.description: Run a focused writing interview that captures rough article fragments in a Markdown file.
skill.summary: Explore writing ideas and save useful fragments before outlining.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The static external-command matches are Markdown fence delimiters inside a file-format example, not executable instructions. The system-reconnaissance match is a benign save-path prompt; I found no prompt injection or malicious intent in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: If the user did not pass a path, ask once where to save the document, then remember it for the rest

finding_verdicts.reason: The flagged text is an opening Markdown code fence for a file-format example, not Ruby or shell execution. The surrounding lines show static sample Markdown content only.
The flagged text is the closing Markdown code fence for the same example. It is not an executable shell construct or instruction to run commands.
Line 13 asks the assistant to ask the user for a save path, which is normal for writing output. It does not enumerate host details, probe the system, or request environmental data.

content.value_statement: Early writing often loses useful lines before a structure exists. This skill runs an exploratory interview and saves promising fragments in one Markdown file.
actual_capabilities: Asks for a save path when one is not provided.
Captures fragments from the first user message.
Creates one working title as the file heading.
Appends fragments separated by horizontal rules.
Re-reads the file before each write to preserve user edits.
Supports user requests to cut, rewrite, or merge fragments.
limitations: Does not create outlines, sections, or final article structure.
Requires a writable Markdown file path for saved fragments.
Does not verify the factual accuracy of captured ideas.
Works best with conversational drafting input.

use_cases.title: Essay Idea Exploration
use_cases.description: Collect rough claims, examples, and lines before deciding the final essay structure.

use_cases.title: Technical Post Discovery
use_cases.description: Interview a developer about a concept and save useful teaching fragments for later drafting.

use_cases.title: Product Narrative Notes
use_cases.description: Gather language, objections, examples, and positioning ideas before preparing a polished narrative.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Fragment File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-fragments. Save to ./fragments.md. Interview me about my topic and capture any strong lines or useful examples.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for starting a new exploratory writing session.

prompt_templates.title: Mine Rough Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-fragments with ./article-fragments.md. I will paste messy notes. Ask follow-up questions and append only the parts worth keeping.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when raw notes need sharper fragments.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Leading Word
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-fragments with ./essay-fragments.md. Push me to name the recurring idea with one strong term, then save candidate phrases and supporting fragments.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the core idea needs a memorable name.

prompt_templates.title: Develop an Existing File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use writing-fragments with ./draft-fragments.md. Re-read the file before each write. Compare new ideas with existing notes and append exploratory material.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for extending a fragment file over multiple sessions.

output_examples.input: I want to write about how small developer tool decisions shape team culture.
output: Working title: Tool Choices Become Team Habits
Fragment: A developer tool is not only a utility. It teaches a team what kinds of work feel normal.
Fragment: The interesting question is not whether the tool is powerful. It is what behavior it makes cheap.

output_examples.input: I have scattered notes about product onboarding and user trust.
output: Working title: Trust Starts Before Activation
Fragment: Onboarding is a promise about how the product will treat the user later.
Fragment: Every skipped explanation is a withdrawal from the user's patience.

best_practices: Provide a file path at the start of the session.
Let the interview stay exploratory before asking for structure.
Review the fragment file between sessions and remove weak material.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to produce a finished article outline.
Do not ask it to overwrite a full draft without a specific edit request.
Do not treat captured fragments as fact-checked publication copy.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates or updates a Markdown file of rough writing fragments.

faq.question: Does it write the final article?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on exploration, not structure or final drafting.

faq.question: Can I use an existing fragment file?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill re-reads the file before writing and preserves existing edits.

faq.question: What kind of input works best?
faq.answer: Use rough thoughts, claims, examples, memories, objections, or half-formed ideas.

faq.question: Does it ask before saving every fragment?
faq.answer: No. It appends useful fragments during the conversation after the save path is known.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
